5. Thread `Principal`, `Bounds`, and `RequestID` into any custom `StepExecutor` that needs them.
6. Regenerate the schema and re-seed `catalog`, `agent`, and `graph`.

## Not in this release

The A2A adapter behind `AgentInvoker` (D5) and the prompt retrofit onto `scoped_binding` (C5), which
is the last item keeping two inheritance mechanisms in the tree. Both are tracked in
[TODO.md](TODO.md).

migrations.title: policy decision point, durable approvals, principal-scoped credentials, and decision records
migrations.summary: The governance wave on top of principals and scoped configuration. A pending approval no longer fails the turn: guardrail.ErrApprovalPending wraps the new domain.ErrApprovalPending instead of ErrForbidden, TurnRuntime suspends the turn with its budget reservation held, and approval.Resumer records the verdict, returns the turn to queued, and re-dispatches it. service/policy adds a fail-closed decision point over the policy statements frozen into a principal's effective release, with obligations the governed tool gateway applies before egress and refuses to skip. Credentials become principal-keyed: credential_binding maps one principal to one scoped identity per tool and purpose, so two agents on the same tool version never share an identity, and every resolution records the authority exercised. domain.AuditEvent is replaced by domain.DecisionRecord with typed identity, authority, policy, outcome, and obligations, and AuditQuery ships the read side. usage_event gains principal and scope attribution. Breaking: AuditSink, ToolCredentialProvider, TurnRecordStore, and TurnLedger.InsertUsageEvent all change shape; ModelRequest gains a principal. Schema grows to fifteen modules and 96 tables with a new approval module, four catalogs, credential_binding, and a rebuilt audit_event.
migrations.body_markdown:
## New packages

| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `contract/policy.go` | `PolicyDecisionPoint`, `PolicyResolver`, `ObligationEnforcer` |
| `contract/approval.go` | `ApprovalStore`, `ApprovalInbox`, `EscalationPolicy`, `Notifier` |
| `domain/decision.go` | `DecisionRecord`, `DecisionSubject`, `Decision`, `Obligation`, `DecisionQuery`, `DecisionPage` |
| `domain/policy.go` | `PolicySet`, `PolicyStatement`, `PolicyEffect` |
| `domain/approval.go` | `ApprovalRequest`, `ApprovalVerdict`, `ApprovalKey`, `ApprovalFilter`, `EscalationStep`, `Notification`, `OutputClass`, `RiskTier` |
| `domain/credential.go` | `CredentialBinding` |
| `service/policy` | `SetEvaluator`, `ReleaseResolver` |
| `service/approval` | `TableStore`, `Gate`, `Resumer`, `BackupEscalation`, `Sweeper`, `ProposalDigest` |

## Interfaces

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `AuditSink.Record(ctx, domain.AuditEvent)` | `Record(ctx, domain.DecisionRecord)` — typed identity, authority, policy, outcome, and obligations instead of an opaque payload |
| — | `AuditQuery.Decisions(ctx, domain.DecisionQuery) (domain.DecisionPage, error)` — the read side ships with the sink |
| `ToolCredentialProvider.Credential(ctx, tenantID, toolID)` | `Credential(ctx, principal, toolID, action, purpose) ([]byte, domain.AuthorityRef, error)` |
| `TurnRecordStore` | adds `Suspend(ctx, tenantID, requestID, reason)` and `Resume(ctx, tenantID, requestID)` |
| `TurnRecordStore.RecordUsage(…, subjectRef, usage)` | `RecordUsage(…, subjectRef, domain.UsageAttribution, usage)` |
| `TurnLedger.InsertUsageEvent(…, subjectRef, usage)` | `InsertUsageEvent(…, subjectRef, domain.UsageAttribution, usage)` |
| — | `contract.PrincipalLimits` — budget and autonomy read from the frozen release |
| — | `contract.CredentialBindingRepository`, `contract.CredentialRevoker` |

## Domain values

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `domain.AuditEvent{TenantID, Category, Payload, OccurredAt}` | removed; use `domain.DecisionRecord` |
| `domain.ModelRequest` | adds `Principal domain.PrincipalRef` for routing attribution and per-agent spend. Provider adapters must not forward it to a vendor |
| `domain.Usage` consumers | new `domain.UsageAttribution{Principal, ScopeID}` accompanies every settled usage event |

New sentinel: `domain.ErrApprovalPending`. `guardrail.ErrApprovalPending` now wraps it instead of `domain.ErrForbidden`, because a pending approval is control flow, not a denial.

## Behavior changes

- **A pending approval no longer fails the turn.** `TurnRuntime` suspends it: the budget reservation stays held, the delivery is acked, and a final frame carries the reason. Settling would resume the turn with no budget; releasing would let a tenant park work to dodge its ceiling.
- **Resuming is a three-step operation.** `approval.Resumer.Resolve` records the verdict, returns the turn to `queued`, and re-dispatches it. A rejection fails the turn instead. Resolving without re-dispatching leaves the turn parked forever, which is why the steps are not separable.
- **`approval.Gate.Decide` is idempotent.** Open is keyed on `(tenant, request, execution_step)`, so a replayed turn re-attaches rather than asking a person twice. `ProposalDigest` binds the verdict to the exact call, and the resolve statement matches on it.
- **`GovernedGateway` gains an optional `Policy`, `Obligations`, `Audit`, and `CredentialPurpose`.** Policy runs after authorization and before guardrails; obligations apply before egress; an obligation with no registered enforcer fails the call with `domain.ErrDegraded`. Every credential resolution records which authority it exercised.
- **Credentials are per principal.** `credential_binding` replaces the shared `tool_version.credential_ref` as the runtime path, so two agents on one tool version resolve different identities.
- **`policy` bindings are statement lists, not string sets.** `scope.PolicyMerger` replaces `SetMerger` for that kind and the new `policy` narrowing rule lets a child drop an allow or add a deny, never add an allow.
- **`usage_event` is attributed.** New `principal_kind`, `principal_id`, and `scope_id` columns make cost reportable per agent and per organizational scope.
- **`AuditCategoryModelRoute` is now `model_route`** (was `model.route`), aligned with `domain.DecisionCategory*`; `guardrail.AuditCategory` is likewise the shared `guardrail` constant.

## Configuration

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `agent_approval_deadline` | 3600 | Seconds a reviewer has before escalation; 0 leaves a request open |
| `agent_credential_ttl` | 300 | Default lifetime of a just-in-time tool credential; a binding's own `MaxTTL` wins when tighter |
| `agent_audit_page_size` | 100 | Decision records per audit query page, clamped to 1000 |

## Schema — one new module, four catalogs, and a rebuilt audit_event

Fifteen modules and 96 Scout tables, up from fourteen and 89.

| Change | Detail |
|---|---|
| New module `approval` | `approval_request`, `approval_decision`; depends on `catalog`, `tenancy`, `agent`, `scope` |
| `catalog` +4 | `decision_outcome`, `approval_status`, `risk_tier`, `output_class`, all seeded |
| `tool` +1 | `credential_binding` |
| `turn_status` +1 seed | `suspended` |
| `audit_event` rebuilt | Typed `principal_*`, `grant_*`, `scope_id`, `action`, `resource`, `release_version`, `policy_*`, `outcome_code`, `obligations`, `reason`, `request_id`, `conversation_id`; `payload_uri`/`payload_digest` become nullable evidence references |
| `usage_event` +3 | `principal_kind`, `principal_id`, `scope_id` |
| `release` depends on `scope` | `audit_event.scope_id` is a real foreign key |

Regenerate with `schema/approval` added to the input list:

```bash
keel="$(go list -m -f '{{.Dir}}' github.com/nauticana/keel)/schema"
go tool schemagen -dialect pgsql \
  -input "${keel}/core,${keel}/geo,${keel}/tenant_management,schema/catalog,schema/tenancy,schema/prompt,schema/model,schema/agent,schema/authorization,schema/scope,schema/approval,schema/tool,schema/graph,schema/knowledge,schema/knowledge_vector,schema/runtime,schema/release,schema/evaluation" \
  -seed "schema/seed/catalog,schema/seed/tenancy,schema/seed/prompt,schema/seed/model,schema/seed/agent,schema/seed/graph,schema/seed/runtime,schema/seed/release" \
  -out build/scout_pgsql.sql
```

## Migration steps

1. Replace every `domain.AuditEvent` construction with `domain.DecisionRecord`, supplying the acting principal — the sink rejects a record without one.
2. Update `ToolCredentialProvider` implementations to the principal-keyed signature and seed `credential_binding` rows; the shared `tool_version.credential_ref` no longer feeds the runtime path.
3. Implement `Suspend`/`Resume` on any custom `TurnRecordStore`, and thread `domain.UsageAttribution` through `RecordUsage`.
4. Wire `approval.Gate` as the `ToolApprovalGate` and `approval.Resumer` into whatever resolves verdicts; a pending approval now suspends rather than failing, so a composition that treated `ErrApprovalPending` as a denial must stop doing so.
5. Register an `ObligationEnforcer` for every obligation your policies emit — an unenforceable obligation now fails the call.
6. Add `schema/approval` to the schemagen input list, re-seed `catalog` and `agent`, and apply.

## Not in this release

The external adapters behind the new ports: OPA or cedar-go behind `PolicyDecisionPoint`, SPIFFE and RFC 8693 behind the credential path, and the OpenTelemetry GenAI mapping. Prompt inheritance also still runs on its own three tables rather than `scoped_binding`. All are tracked in [TODO.md](TODO.md).

migrations.title: principals, scoped configuration inheritance, and compiled effective releases
migrations.summary: Scout gains the two primitives an enterprise agent-organization control plane needs and did not have: a principal that names the acting subject of every governed operation, and a generic scoped-inheritance compiler that freezes effective configuration with provenance. domain.Principal carries kind, id, tenant, scope, pinned release, entitlements digest, and an RFC 8693-shaped authority chain, and threads through TurnRequest, ToolCall, KnowledgeQuery, GuardrailSubject, SafetyEvent, and Observation. The governed tool gateway now rejects a zero principal and enforces agent_tool_binding at invoke time through the new BindingAuthorizer. Agents attach to keel RBAC through a new agent_permission table mirroring user_permission, so agents and humans evaluate through one authorization model rather than two. A new scope module adds scope, scoped_binding, and effective_agent_release: one binding table for every resource kind, sealed clauses set by the parent scope, and a narrowing checker that rejects any child binding that broadens what it inherits. Breaking: ToolCall, TurnRequest, TenantContext, KnowledgeQuery, GuardrailSubject, SafetyEvent, and Observation all change shape. Schema grows from twelve modules and 82 tables to fourteen and 89.
migrations.body_markdown:
## New packages

| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `contract/principal.go` | `PrincipalResolver`, `ExternalPrincipalSource`, `PrincipalAuthorizer`, `DelegationVerifier` |
| `contract/scope.go` | `ScopeRepository`, `ResourceMerger`, `ResourceMergerRegistry`, `NarrowingChecker`, `EffectiveConfigCompiler`, `EffectiveReleaseRepository` |
| `domain/principal.go` | `Principal`, `PrincipalRef`, `PrincipalKind`, `AuthorityChain`, `AuthorityHop`, `AuthorityRef`, `AuthorizationGrant` |
| `domain/scope.go` | `Scope`, `ScopeChain`, `ScopedBinding`, `ResourceKind`, `MergeMode`, `AutonomyMode`, `Provenance`, `EffectiveResource`, `EffectiveRelease`, `CompileRequest` |
| `service/principal` | `RoleAuthorizer`, `TableResolver`, `ChainVerifier` |
| `service/scope` | `Compiler`, `MergerRegistry`, `LatticeChecker`, `TableScopeRepository`, `TableEffectiveReleaseStore`, `Digest` |

## Domain values

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `domain.ToolCall{TenantContext, RequestID, ConversationID, ToolID, ToolVersion, Arguments}` | adds `Principal domain.Principal`; `GovernedGateway` rejects a zero principal and a principal whose tenant does not own the call |
| `domain.TurnRequest{TenantContext, RequestID, ConversationID, AgentID, Input}` | adds `Principal domain.Principal` and `OnBehalfOf domain.PrincipalRef` |
| `domain.TenantContext` | adds `ScopeID`, the tenant scope-tree node the work belongs to |
| `domain.KnowledgeQuery.Principal string` | `domain.KnowledgeQuery.Principal domain.Principal` — the caller-asserted string is gone; use `.ID` where a display value is needed |
| `domain.GuardrailSubject` | adds `Principal domain.PrincipalRef` |
| `domain.SafetyEvent` | adds `Principal domain.PrincipalRef` |
| `domain.Observation` | adds `Principal domain.PrincipalRef` and `ScopeID`; both are exact ledger dimensions and must never become metric labels |

New sentinels in `domain/errors.go`: `ErrPrincipalUnknown`, `ErrAuthorityExceeded`, `ErrDelegationDepth`, `ErrGrantExpired`, `ErrSealed`.

## Behavior changes

- `toolgateway.GovernedGateway.validate` now requires a resolved principal on every call, including the construction-time probe. A composition that built calls without one fails with `domain.ErrPrincipalUnknown`.
- `toolgateway.BindingAuthorizer` is the reference `contract.ToolAuthorizer`: it lists the calling principal's pinned release through `ToolRegistry.List` and rejects any tool the release does not bind, at that exact version. Tenant ownership of a tool no longer implies an agent may call it.
- `controlplane.AgentPublisher` gains optional `Effective`, `Releases`, and `ScopeID`. Set together, publication compiles the scope chain and stores an `effective_agent_release`; a binding that broadens what it inherits fails publication with `domain.ErrAuthorityExceeded`, and a sealed parent binding fails with `domain.ErrSealed`.
- `scope.Compiler` checks the **merged** result against what it inherited, so a `replace` that grants more and an `append` that widens a set fail the same comparison. `BudgetMerger` and `AutonomyMerger` additionally clamp to the tighter inherited value.
- `scope.LatticeChecker` fails closed on a resource kind with no narrowing rule, and `MergerRegistry` fails closed on a kind with no merger.

## Configuration

Two flags, seeded into `application_config_flag` by the `agent` module:

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `agent_max_scope_depth` | 8 | Longest scope chain a release may compile over |
| `agent_max_delegation_hops` | 4 | Longest authority chain a principal may present |

## Schema — two new modules and three new catalogs

`schema/` grows from twelve to fourteen modules; the full set is 89 Scout tables instead of 82.

| Module | Tables | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| `authorization` | `agent_permission` | `agent` |
| `scope` | `scope`, `scoped_binding`, `effective_agent_release` | `catalog`, `tenancy`, `agent` |

`catalog` gains `scope_kind`, `resource_kind`, and `merge_mode`, all seeded. Scout seeds only the `tenant` root scope kind; a product names its own levels below it.

`agent_permission` mirrors keel's `user_permission`, including `begda`/`endda`, so agents and humans evaluate through the same `authorization_role_permission` grants and the same `low_limit`/`high_limit` bounds. Agents are deliberately not rows in `user_account`.

Regenerate with the two new modules in the input list:

```bash
keel="$(go list -m -f '{{.Dir}}' github.com/nauticana/keel)/schema"
go tool schemagen -dialect pgsql \
  -input "${keel}/core,${keel}/geo,${keel}/tenant_management,schema/catalog,schema/tenancy,schema/prompt,schema/model,schema/agent,schema/authorization,schema/scope,schema/tool,schema/graph,schema/knowledge,schema/knowledge_vector,schema/runtime,schema/release,schema/evaluation" \
  -seed "schema/seed/catalog,schema/seed/tenancy,schema/seed/prompt,schema/seed/model,schema/seed/agent,schema/seed/graph,schema/seed/runtime,schema/seed/release" \
  -out build/scout_pgsql.sql
```

## Migration steps

1. Resolve a `domain.Principal` at every entry point and set it on `TurnRequest` and `ToolCall`; a zero principal is rejected, not defaulted.
2. Replace `KnowledgeQuery.Principal` string assignments with a `domain.Principal`.
3. Inject `toolgateway.BindingAuthorizer` (or an equivalent principal-aware `ToolAuthorizer`) and confirm every agent release binds the tools it calls.
4. Add the `authorization` and `scope` modules to the schemagen input list, re-seed `catalog` and `agent`, and apply.
5. Optionally wire `scope.Compiler` and `scope.TableEffectiveReleaseStore` into `AgentPublisher` to freeze effective configuration at publication.

## Not in this release

Prompt inheritance still uses `prompt_baseline`, `tenant_prompt_default`, and `agent_prompt_override` rather than `scoped_binding`. Retrofitting it, and the wave-2 blocks that consume these primitives — policy decision point, durable approvals, principal-scoped credentials, scope-keyed budgets, decision records — are tracked in [TODO.md](TODO.md).

migrations.title: reference mechanisms behind the data-plane, knowledge, evaluation, and rollout contracts
migrations.summary: Scout ships the mechanisms its contracts previously only declared: a policy model router with resilient and hedged gateways, the durable turn slice (ingress, queue, fair scheduler, dead letters, runtime, session store, step idempotency) with conformance suites, chunk-aware knowledge ingestion and a pgvector index that compiles entitlements into the query, a quality-evaluation pipeline issuing signed expiring gate decisions, a rollout controller with pin precedence and release bundles, a layered stateful guardrail enforcer with a fenced tool circuit breaker, bounded-cardinality observability, and a distributed limiter with a latency-budget allocator. Breaking: contract/release_and_observability.go splits into release.go and observability.go; StepIdempotencyStore takes domain.ExecutionStep; ConversationRuntime.HandleTurn takes domain.TurnDispatch; KnowledgeVectorIndex indexes chunks and gains Remove; StepCheckpoint drops CheckpointID and RequestID for ExecutionStepID, IdempotencyKey, Fingerprint, and StateRef; GuardrailConfig requires RulesDigest. Schema adds the knowledge and evaluation groups, the durable turn queue, rollout state and pins, and a PostgreSQL-only chunk vector table. The schema is also reorganized from five groups into twelve selectable modules so a downstream creates only the tables it uses — a Studio-only install is 27 Scout tables instead of 82 — with byte-identical DDL and seed output for the full set.
migrations.body_markdown:
## Contract files

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `contract/release_and_observability.go` | `contract/release.go` (compatibility runs, rollout) and `contract/observability.go` (audit sink, runtime metrics) |

Every interface keeps its name; only the file split. New files: `contract/evaluation.go`, `contract/guardrail.go` additions, `contract/data_plane.go` additions.

## Domain values

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `domain.StepCheckpoint{CheckpointID, RequestID, ...}` | `domain.StepCheckpoint{ExecutionStepID, IdempotencyKey, Fingerprint, StateRef, ...}` — `CheckpointID` and `RequestID` are gone; the row is keyed by (tenant, conversation, turn, step) and the state pointer is an `ObjectRef` |
| `domain.ExecutionStep{StepID, ...}` | adds `ExecutionStepID int64`, the compiled `execution_step.id` persistence keys on; `StepID` stays the logical name |
| `domain.SessionSnapshot{State, ...}` | adds `LatestTurnNo`, `LatestStepNo`, `StateRef` |
| `domain.ModelSelection{Provider, Model, CapacityPool}` | adds `ModelVersion`, `Region`, `RouteID`, `RoutingGeneration`, `Reason` |
| `domain.ModelRequest` | adds `RequiredCapabilities`, `AffinityKey`, `Idempotent`, `ExcludedRouteIDs` |
| `domain.TenantContext` | adds `Tier` and `Region`, the bounded labels fleet metrics may carry |
| `domain.GuardrailConfig{Version, Rules}` | adds `RulesDigest`; runtime recomputes it and fails closed on mismatch, so publishers must set `guardrail.Digest(rules)` |
| `domain.KnowledgeDocument` | adds `SourceVersion`, `Entitlements`, `RedactionPolicyVersion` |
| `domain.KnowledgeQuery` | adds `Embedding` for a caller that already embedded the query |
| `domain.KnowledgeMatch` | adds `ChunkID`, `SourceVersion`, `StartOffset`, `EndOffset` |
| `domain.RolloutHealth` | adds `Breach`, `EffectSize`, `Confidence`, `TelemetryFreshAt` |
| `domain.Observation` (new) | stage- and version-attributed measurement replacing ad-hoc log reconstruction |

New value files: `domain/object.go` (`ObjectRef`), `domain/observation.go`, `domain/evaluation.go`. New sentinels in `domain/errors.go`: `ErrDeadlineInfeasible`, `ErrNoRoute`, `ErrStaleEvidence`, `ErrDegraded`, and `ErrBudgetSettled` — a `TenantBudgetManager.Reserve` that finds the request already settled returns it so a redelivery replays instead of double-charging.

## Interfaces

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `StepIdempotencyStore.Begin/Commit/Abandon(ctx, tenantID, requestID, stepID string)` | `...(ctx, tenantID, requestID string, step domain.ExecutionStep)` — the store needs the compiled `ExecutionStepID` to write the FK |
| `ConversationRuntime.HandleTurn(ctx, domain.TurnRequest)` | `HandleTurn(ctx, domain.TurnDispatch)` — the runtime executes a delivery and needs its reply route; the request is `dispatch.Turn` |
| `KnowledgeVectorIndex.Index(ctx, document, embedding)` | `Index(ctx, items []domain.ChunkEmbedding)` plus `Remove(ctx, tenantID, kb, version, documentID)` — the index stores chunks, not whole documents |
| `runtime.canarySelected(tenantID, aliasID, conversationID, percentage)` | `release.CanarySelected(tenantID, key, conversationID, percentage)` |
| `isolation.EntitlementBudgetPolicy.now` | `EntitlementBudgetPolicy.Now func() time.Time` |

`contract.GuardrailEnforcer`, `contract.ToolCircuitBreaker`, and `contract.RuntimeMetrics` are unchanged; the new stateful and structured behavior arrives as optional capabilities (`StreamingGuardrail`, `FencedToolCircuitBreaker`, `ObservationRecorder`) a value may also implement.

## Behavior changes

- `runtime.PublishedAgentResolver` gains `Versions contract.AgentVersionTrafficManager`; when set it owns version choice. Its named query `scout_runtime_published_agent` selects one more column (`p.agent_id`) and a new query `scout_runtime_published_agent_version` loads a pinned off-deployment definition — update any query fake.
- `SessionCoordinator.Checkpoint`/`Complete` accept `expectedRevision == 0` (the legitimate "no snapshot yet" state) and now invalidate the cache on durable-write failure as well as success.
- `memcache.MemorySessionCache.Put` rejects a negative revision and ignores a put older than the cached one.
- `dataplane.MemoryCacheConfig` gains `RemoteTTL`; a local `TTL` greater than a non-zero `RemoteTTL` now fails construction.
- `toolgateway.GovernedGateway` wraps tool-result validation failures in `ErrInvalidToolOutput` and gates breaker recording behind `ToolFailureClassifier`, so cancellation and typed validation or authorization errors no longer trip a dependency breaker.
- `knowledge.BatchingEmbedder` and `dataplane.MemoryReplyHub` expose an idempotent `Close`; calls after it return `domain.ErrConflict`.
- A failed or cancelled turn settles the usage already produced and releases only a hold with no usage behind it, so provider work stays metered when a turn ends badly.
- `KnowledgeVectorIndex` search requires a `knowledge_document_manifest` row naming the chunk's version as active and untombstoned; a document with no manifest is invisible rather than unfiltered.
- Negative limits are rejected at construction instead of silently defaulting: `BudgetLedger.ReservationTTL`, `MemoryLoopDetector.Window`/`MaxFingerprints`, `WindowedCostBreaker.Buckets`, `BatchingEmbedder.MaxBatch`/`MaxWait`/`Timeout`, and the `MemoryReplyHub` limits.
- Services that read wall time now take an injected `Now func() time.Time`: `controlplane.StudioService`, `runtime.BaseDraftTester`, `isolation.EntitlementBudgetPolicy`. Nil keeps `time.Now`.

## Schema — modules replace the five groups

`schema/` is now twelve selectable modules instead of five groups, so a downstream generates only what its product uses. `control_plane` is gone; its 30 tables are split by concern. No table was renamed, dropped, or altered — the full generated DDL and seed output are byte-identical to the previous layout.

| Old group | New module(s) |
|---|---|
| `catalog` | `catalog` (unchanged) |
| `tenancy` | `tenancy` (unchanged) |
| `control_plane` | `prompt` (2), `model` (5), `agent` (9), `tool` (4), `graph` (4), `knowledge` (5 of 8), `knowledge_vector` (1) |
| `knowledge` | merged into `knowledge` |
| `runtime` | `runtime`, plus new `turn_queue` and `turn_dead_letter` |
| `release` | `release`, plus rollout state, transitions, bypasses, bundles, pins, cohorts, and conversation release identity |
| — | `evaluation` (new, 10 tables) |

Seed files move with their module: `schema/seed/control_plane.yml` splits into `schema/seed/{catalog,prompt,model,agent,graph,runtime}/`, and `schema/seed/{tenancy,release}.yml` become `schema/seed/{tenancy,release}/`. Each seed file inserts only into its own module's tables.

Regenerate with the module list and the matching seed directories:

```bash
keel="$(go list -m -f '{{.Dir}}' github.com/nauticana/keel)/schema"
go tool schemagen -dialect pgsql \
  -input "${keel}/core,${keel}/geo,${keel}/tenant_management,schema/catalog,schema/tenancy,schema/prompt,schema/model,schema/agent,schema/tool,schema/graph,schema/knowledge,schema/knowledge_vector,schema/runtime,schema/release,schema/evaluation" \
  -seed "schema/seed/catalog,schema/seed/tenancy,schema/seed/prompt,schema/seed/model,schema/seed/agent,schema/seed/graph,schema/seed/runtime,schema/seed/release" \
  -out build/scout_pgsql.sql
```

Two traps when trimming the list: seeding a module you did not install emits inserts into a table that was never created, and pointing `-seed` at the parent `schema/seed` directory silently seeds nothing because the generator does not descend into subdirectories.

New tables to apply, on top of the previous layout: `turn_queue`, `turn_dead_letter`, `knowledge_chunk_vector` (PostgreSQL-only: `VECTOR`, `TSVECTOR`, `JSONB`), the `knowledge` module's `knowledge_document_manifest`, `knowledge_base_alias`, `knowledge_source_event`, the `release` module's `rollout_stage`, `release_bundle`, `platform_rollout_state`, `platform_rollout_transition`, `platform_rollout_bypass`, `agent_version_pin`, `experiment_cohort`, `conversation_release`, and the whole `evaluation` module. Apply the `rollout_stage` seed before `platform_rollout_state`, which references it. `knowledge_chunk_vector` additionally needs `CREATE EXTENSION vector` and one `PgVectorIndex.EnsureIndexes(ctx, dimensions)` call per embedding width.

## Migration steps

1. Split imports of `contract/release_and_observability.go` — no code change, the package is still flat.
2. Set `RulesDigest` on every published `GuardrailConfig` and reload guardrail policy rows.
3. Update `StepIdempotencyStore` and `ConversationRuntime` call sites to pass `domain.ExecutionStep` and `domain.TurnDispatch`.
4. Rework any `KnowledgeVectorIndex` implementation to index `[]domain.ChunkEmbedding` and implement `Remove`.
5. Drop reads of `StepCheckpoint.CheckpointID`/`RequestID`; carry the compiled `ExecutionStepID` and an `IdempotencyKey` instead.
6. Repoint the schemagen `-input` and `-seed` lists at the modules your product uses, regenerate both dialects, apply the new tables and seeds, then deploy.
7. Optional but recommended: inject `Observer` into `StreamPump` and `HybridRetriever`, and a `contract.AgentVersionTrafficManager` into `PublishedAgentResolver`.
